title: Get GMet's daily forecast on WhatsApp
summary: The Ghana Meteorological Agency publishes forecasts every day and shares them on its WhatsApp channel, so you can plan around hot afternoons.
details: Follow the GMet WhatsApp channel or check meteo.gov.gh for the 24-hour forecast.
GMet issues daily forecasts three times a day: 05:00, 11:00 and 17:00.
GMet is also on X (@GhanaMet) and Facebook (GMetForecastOffice).

title: Keep food safe in hot weather
summary: Food spoils fast in Accra's heat. The Food and Drugs Authority's hot-weather guide gives simple rules for households, cooks and market sellers.
details: Keep meat, dairy, fruit, vegetables and cooked meals refrigerated at or below 4°C.
Don't leave food at room temperature for more than two hours, or one hour when it is above 32°C.
Cook meat, poultry and seafood to 75°C inside, and reheat leftovers to the same temperature.
Sellers: keep meat, fish and dairy in insulated coolers or boxes with ice.

sources.title: Food and Drugs Authority Ghana: Food handling during hot weather

title: Call 112 for a heat emergency
summary: If someone becomes seriously unwell in extreme heat, call the National Ambulance Service on 112. It's free from any network.
details: Call 112: the national emergency hotline, free from any network, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
Don't use the website contact form for a medical emergency.
Non-emergency enquiries: 0501614877 or 0505982870, Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

sources.title: National Ambulance Service Ghana: Contact us

title: Check GMet's daily air quality forecast
summary: The Ghana Meteorological Agency publishes a free PM2.5 (fine dust and smoke) forecast for the whole country every day. Check it before outdoor exercise.
details: Forecasts are listed newest first on the GMet air quality page.
Levels are given as Good, Moderate, Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups or Unhealthy.
There's also a map view at meteo.gov.gh/mapviewer.

sources.title: Ghana Meteorological Agency: PM2.5 Air Quality Forecast
Ghana Meteorological Agency: Air quality forecasting

title: See live air quality across Accra's neighbourhoods
summary: IQAir shows hourly air quality readings for Accra from local monitoring stations, with health advice for each level. It's useful for checking your own area.
details: The page lists the most polluted stations in Accra right now.
When air is moderate or worse, sensitive groups should reduce outdoor exercise.
Close your windows to keep dirty outdoor air out.
Sensitive groups should wear a mask outdoors.

title: Report smoke, dust or noise nuisance to AMA
summary: AMA's Metro Public Health Department monitors smoke, dust and noise nuisance in the city. If it's affecting your home or street, let AMA know.
details: The department's environmental monitoring covers smoke, dust and noise nuisance.
Noise complaints are made at the Metro Public Health Department.
For smoke or dust, contact AMA on 0302 665 951 or info@ama.gov.gh.

sources.title: Accra Metropolitan Assembly: Environmental Health Services

title: Save NADMO's flood emergency numbers
summary: The National Disaster Management Organisation (NADMO) handles floods and other disasters. Save its numbers before the rain comes.
details: 112: emergency, 24/7.
0302964884: national emergency line, free from all networks.
0291913077: NADMO emergency, 24/7.
WhatsApp: 0204 833 556.

title: Report flooding to NADMO online or on WhatsApp
summary: You can report a flood or other disaster on NADMO's online map, with a photo and location, so responders know where help is needed.
details: Use the Report Disaster form on the NADMO map page. Choose 'Flood' as the type.
Add a description, the region and the location. A photo is optional (JPEG or PNG, up to 5MB).
You can also report on WhatsApp: 0204 833 556.
For life-threatening emergencies, call 112 instead.

sources.title: NADMO: Disaster map and report form

title: Get GMet's storm and rain warnings
summary: The Ghana Meteorological Agency posts official warnings for rainstorms and thunderstorms. Sign up to get forecasts and alerts by email.
details: Current and past warnings are listed on the GMet alerts page.
Sign up on meteo.gov.gh to receive forecasts, alerts and flood monitoring bulletins in your inbox.
GMet also has a WhatsApp community for updates.

title: Report a blocked drain to AMA
summary: Choked drains are a big cause of Accra's floods. Report blocked drains, gutters or culverts, or flooding, on the AMA's citizen feedback form.
details: Choose 'Drains/gutters', 'Culverts' or 'Flooding' as the category.
Add the location's Ghana Post GPS digital address and, if you can, a photo.
AMA phone: 0302 665 951.

title: Sign up with an AMA-accredited waste collector
summary: Every home and business in Accra must subscribe to a waste collection service. Using an AMA-accredited collector keeps rubbish out of drains and away from burning.
details: Subscription to solid waste collection is mandatory for all owners and occupiers of premises.
Register only with an AMA-accredited service provider in your community. Using unaccredited providers is illegal.
Charges are set each year in the AMA Fee Fixing Resolution.
Ask AMA for help: 0302 665 951 or info@ama.gov.gh.

sources.title: Accra Metropolitan Assembly: Waste Management Services

title: Report uncollected rubbish or an illegal dump
summary: If refuse isn't being collected or someone has started a dump site, report it to the AMA so it's cleared before it's burned or washed into drains.
details: Use the AMA citizen feedback form and choose 'Uncollected Refuse' or 'Illegal Dumpsite'.
Add the Ghana Post GPS digital address and a photo if you can.
Or call AMA: 0302 665 951.

title: Arrange removal of building debris or e-waste
summary: The AMA waste department offers special collections for construction debris and e-waste, and septic tank emptying, so these don't end up dumped or burned.
details: Special waste evacuation covers construction debris and e-waste.
Liquid waste services include septic tank desludging.
Contact AMA: 0302 665 951 or info@ama.gov.gh.

sources.title: Accra Metropolitan Assembly: Waste Management Services

title: Join National Sanitation Day
summary: On the first Saturday of every month, communities across Ghana clean streets and clear drains together. Clear drains mean less flooding when the rains come.
details: National Sanitation Day is held on the first Saturday of every month in all assemblies.
Clean your home and surroundings, clear litter from public spaces and join your community clean-up.
The next one should be Saturday 7 November 2026. Check AMA's news page for local start times.
